items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: way before that, in 1950 I believe there was a dance band, Les Brown’s band with Bob Hope.

ctx.x: So Teddy Wilson — now I think I had read that you had a chance encounter with Oscar Peterson?

Yes. The first great pianist I had met actually in person was Oscar Peterson. That was in 1953 I believe. That was the first time the American jazz group came to Japan for the Japanese audience. Before that a few groups came to Japan but they were for the USO © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

tour for the American troops. For example, Louis Armstrong was there one time, and the Gene Krupa Trio was there one time, and way before that, in 1950 I believe there was a dance band, Les Brown’s band with Bob Hope. But more than anything, I think ’51, I’m not quite sure, there is Oscar Pettiford the leader, and J.J. Johnson and Howard McGhee, they were also on the USO tour. And Charlie Rice, the drummer, I forgot the name of the guitar player, they didn’t have a pianist for the USO tour, because the piano you…

items.q: Les Brown and Bob Hope came for a USO tour and they played at the stadium in Yokohama and uh … for the Americans, you know, you [Japanese] couldn‟t get in there. But I kind of snuck in there

ctx.x: Uh, it was called Brückner. I think it was called Brückner. And, uh … it really didn‟t matter to me, whatever, it was okay. But that was called Brückner and…. Soon after I bought the piano, the Blue Coats were playing at a Yokohama place, a civilian club, called the Colonial Club, called Club Colonial, a civilian club. Les Brown and Bob Hope came for a USO tour and they played at the stadium in Yokohama and uh … for the Americans, you know, you [Japanese] couldn‟t get in there. But I kind of snuck in there…
“I‟ve Got My Love to Keep Me Warm.”
